title: Enhanced two-photon sources in a cavity-coupled two-atom system
authors: Zhicai Chen, Jun Xu, Deyi Kong, Xiangming Hu, Fei Wang
abstract: We propose a component-selective scheme for improving two-photon sources in a cavity-coupled two-atom system, where a single cavity mode interacts with two two-level atoms driven by phase-controlled classical fields of the same frequency. By controlling the atomic detunings and driving phase, the system can be tailored toward optimized cavity-field two-photon blockade or strongly correlated fluorescence photon-pair emission. When the two-cavity-photon component is enhanced, the cavity field exhibits optimized two-photon blockade with simultaneous suppression of unwanted one- and three-photon components at a comparable two-photon population. In another parameter regime, strongly correlated fluorescence photon pairs can also be generated from the two atoms by selecting the double-atomic-excitation component in the same two-excitation manifold. This approach provides a route toward high-quality and versatile two-photon sources, with potential applications in few-photon quantum optics and quantum information processing.
summary: The paper proposes a component-selective scheme for enhancing two-photon sources in a cavity coupled to two atoms. By precisely controlling atomic detunings and driving phases, the system can be tuned to exhibit optimized two-photon blockade or generate strongly correlated fluorescence photon pairs. This offers a versatile route for high-quality quantum light sources.
main_problem: The goal is to improve two-photon sources by achieving component-selective control in a cavity-coupled two-atom system, moving beyond simple blockade realization.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that controlling atomic detunings and the relative driving phase allows for optimized cavity-field two-photon blockade or the generation of strongly correlated fluorescence photon pairs independently.
method: Theoretical analysis involves diagonalizing Hamiltonians in fixed excitation number subspaces, coupled with numerical simulation of correlation functions using the Lindblad master equation.
model_or_system: The system is a single cavity mode interacting with two two-level atoms, driven by phase-controlled classical fields. The Hamiltonian includes terms for detuning, atom-cavity interaction, and driving fields.
key_observables: Two-photon blockade ($g^{(2)}_{cav}(0) > 1$ and $g^{(3)}_{cav}(0) < 1$), strongly correlated fluorescence photon pairs ($g^{(2)}_{12}(0)$), and the double-atomic-excitation probability ($	ext{Pee}$).
important_parameters: Atomic detunings ($\Delta_j$) and relative driving phase ($\phi$); resonance conditions derived from $\det(H_2) = 0$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on component-selective control by tuning parameters to optimize specific excitation components, distinguishing between cavity photon blockade and fluorescence pair generation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate correlation functions ($g^{(2)}, g^{(3)}$) vs. detuning, showing blockade regimes; other figures map the interplay between $g^{(2)}_{12}(0)$ and $	ext{Pee}$ across different detuning cuts to find optimal operating points.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the general Hamiltonian and methods for analyzing photon statistics in two-atom systems. It then details how component selectivity is achieved by tuning parameters to optimize either cavity blockade or fluorescence pair generation, comparing these distinct physical mechanisms.
why_interesting: This work provides a sophisticated example of using engineered light-matter interactions (cavity QED) to achieve highly controlled nonclassical light sources, which is central to quantum optics and quantum information processing.
